title: An unparseable date comparand on a datetime filter is passed through and compares false — HTTP 200, zero rows, no diagnostic — while an unknown `{placeholder}` is correctly rejected 400 (17.0.0 GA)
body:
Found while probing objectstack-ai/hotcrm#520 to closure (dispatched from hotcrm#1153). Filed separately because it is a **different cause with the same visual symptom** as that card, and folding it in would have made a clean close dishonest. Measured on `@objectstack/*` **17.0.0 GA**, `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query`.

## The asymmetry

Two kinds of unusable comparand on a `datetime` field, two completely different treatments:

```
--- comparands the API cannot take literally ---
  $gte "last_30_days"        HTTP 200  case_count=0
  created_date: "last_30_days"  (bare equality)   HTTP 200  case_count=0
  $gte "not-a-date-at-all"   HTTP 200  case_count=0
  $gte ""                    HTTP 200  case_count=38    <- treated as "no constraint"

--- placeholder comparands ---
  $gte "{30_days_ago}"       HTTP 200  case_count=38    (correct — resolves to start of day)
  $gte "{TODAY}"             HTTP 400  FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN
  $gte "{not_a_token}"       HTTP 400  FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN
```

Ground truth on that dataset: 51 rows total, 38 within a start-of-day 30-days-ago floor.

A `{placeholder}` the resolver does not know is **rejected loudly**, with a message listing the resolvable tokens — exactly right. A **bare string** that is not a date is not validated at all: it is bound as-is, the comparison is false for every row, and the caller receives `HTTP 200` with an empty result set and nothing to indicate the filter was meaningless.

`""` is a third behaviour again — it silently drops the constraint and returns everything, which is the opposite direction of wrong.

## Why it is worth a card

An empty chart is the hardest failure to debug: it is indistinguishable from "there is genuinely no data", and it is the exact user-visible shape of hotcrm#520 (*"customer-service dashboard renders blank"*), which cost that project a workaround, a CI guard and three separate re-measurements over three weeks before the underlying driver bug was found.

The relative-date vocabulary makes it concretely reachable rather than theoretical: `last_7_days` / `last_30_days` / `last_90_days` are real, declared preset names in the dashboard schema. The shipped console lowers them to `{N_days_ago}` / `{today}` macros before they reach this API, so the console path is safe — but any other caller that has the preset name in hand (a saved report, an integration, an MCP client, an AI-authored query) sends the name itself and gets a silent zero back. The vocabulary is declared in one layer and unrecognised in the next, with no error at the boundary.

The fix direction that matches how placeholders are already handled: **reject a comparand that a temporal field cannot interpret**, with the same shape as `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` — the machinery, the message style and the precedent all exist a few lines away. Extending it to non-placeholder strings on a temporal target is the small half; deciding what `""` should mean on a temporal filter is the other, and today it means something different again.

## Repro

```
POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query
{"datasetName":"<any dataset over an object with a datetime field>",
 "selection":{"measures":["<count measure>"],
              "runtimeFilter":{"<datetime field>":{"$gte":"last_30_days"}}}}
-> 200, zero rows, no diagnostic
```

Swap the comparand for `"{not_a_token}"` to see the loud path the same request takes when the value merely happens to be wrapped in braces.
